source_text:
Fragmentum in epistulam ii ad Thessalonicenses
2 Thess 2,78 Ὅταν μέντοι τὸ πέρας ἐπιστῇ τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ προθεσμίας, καὶ ὁ
νῦν κατέχων αὐτὸν ὅρος ἐκστῇ πληρωθείς, ἑτοίμως τότε καὶ δίχα πάσης ἀναβολῆς ὁ
ἄνομος ἀποκαλυφθήσεται.
thought_title: The appointed end and the removal of the boundary
orientation: Gennadius is commenting on 2 Thessalonians 2:7-8, explaining when and how the lawless one will be revealed.
pass_a_gloss: But when the end of the appointed time of God arrives, and the boundary that now restrains the lawless one is removed, its purpose fulfilled, then immediately and without any delay the lawless one will be revealed.

choices.english: the boundary that now restrains him
choices.why: The glossary requires 'boundary' for ὅρος and 'what now restrains' for ὁ κατέχων; rendering the participle as a relative clause keeps the present restraining force clear while preserving the noun boundary as the subject.
rejected: the boundary now holding him back

choices.why: ἐκστῇ is aorist subjunctive of ἐξίστημι, meaning to withdraw or step aside; πληρωθείς is an aorist passive participle agreeing with ὅρος, indicating the boundary's appointed role is completed before it withdraws.

choices.term: ἑτοίμως τότε καὶ δίχα πάσης ἀναβολῆς
choices.english: then readily and without any delay
choices.why: ἑτοίμως means readily or promptly, and δίχα πάσης ἀναβολῆς is literally 'apart from all delay'; the double emphasis on immediacy is preserved.
rejected: then promptly and with no postponement
then readily and apart from every delay

choices.term: τὸ πέρας ἐπιστῇ τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ προθεσμίας
choices.english: the end of the appointed time of God arrives
choices.why: The genitive τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ προθεσμίας modifies πέρας; the word order 'of the appointed time of God' keeps the genitive chain literal while remaining readable.
rejected: the end of God's appointed time arrives
the limit of the divine appointed period comes

pass_b_english: But when the end of God's appointed time arrives, and the boundary that now restrains the lawless one, its purpose fulfilled, is removed, then the lawless one will be revealed immediately and without any delay.
notes: The source notation '2 Thess 2,78' appears to be a typographical error or unusual notation, likely intended as 2:7-8 or 2:7,8.

last_rejected.why: 'ἐκστῇ' means 'removed/taken away,' not voluntary 'steps aside'; changes agency and manner.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐκστῇ (from ἐφίστημι/ἐξίστημι) can mean 'step away/aside'; 'steps aside' is within normal range, not a major error.
